evidence: sheets/<id>.png (row1 desktop start/mid/finish/reveal, row2 phone), metrics.json, catalog_A/B rows, plus a live 390x844 DOM probe of the action controls (/tmp/quality/b1_probe.mjs)
shared_findings: Phone (all 14 games): the header title is clipped to 'MOTIONAL RELEASE CONSO…' and the LVL badge sits on top of it. The mic icon covers the end of the input text ('my boss yelled at me and I fe…').

Phone (CRACK, STOMP, ZAP, MELT, SHRED, FLUSH, BURN, VACUUM): the main action control is drawn under the Live Guide card, so it is invisible. In the probe the control rects (y 606-704) sit inside the guide rect (27,583 336x125). Taps still pass through to it, but the player cannot see it.

Every game ends on the same reveal card ('RELEASE COMPLETE / NAME / CALMER ✓ … / FEEL A SHIFT?') over an empty dark backdrop. The card has no character and nothing from the game. On desktop it is small (about 265 px wide in a 1280 frame). In the desktop reveal tiles for 1, 6, 16 and 19 the card is missing: only the PREVIOUS and NEXT pills show.

Characters show up only as blurred, low-opacity static decals around the stage edges. In POP and STOMP, tiny character heads also appear as finale confetti. No game has an in-world character that reacts.
On phone, user words render at about 8-10 px against the required 15 px. The '+STILL HIT · CHAIN ×N' toast pill regularly covers bubbles or guide text.

Perf: under headless software rendering every game exceeds p95 > 34 ms and max > 120 ms. Heap growth stays under 8 MB and there are no errors. Relative outliers: UNHOOK desktop (p95 2100 ms, 0.6 fps, 25.6 s of long tasks), a 2974 ms long task on BURN phone, a 1775 ms long task on SWIPE phone, SHRED desktop p95 1150 ms, and an ERASE desktop long task of 1478 ms.
